title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering and workflow constraints, and group-level safety). Prior work documents prototype intent→configuration systems and advocates verifier/validator stages, but artifact-grounded evidence quantifying generator→verifier→repair pipelines in a tightly controlled experimental design is limited [1],[2],[3].

This study asks the preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not measure the effect of independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Detailed reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution bundle and deterministic reconciliation.
sections.related_work:
Recent NetOps and AIOps work shows active research on intent-driven configuration synthesis and prototype generator–validator pipelines [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain literature in program repair and generate→validate→repair demonstrates that verifier-assisted repair can materially improve correctness when the oracle is well-specified; such designs motivate guarded pipelines in operational settings [4],[5],[6]. Surveys on agentic AI and LLM safety emphasize hallucination/confabulation failure modes and recommend verifier gates, provenance, and constrained tool access for operational workflows [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap positioning. The supplied literature documents prototype systems and advocate verification, but few verified, preregistered paired experiments isolate the marginal repair effect under shared-initial semantics. Our artifact-grounded experiment directly addresses this narrower empirical gap by reusing identical initial candidates across baseline and guarded episodes, allowing the guarded outcome to differ only when the deterministic verifier issues and applies a repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before observing model outputs. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The protocol fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. The preregistration, sampling plan, and analysis plan are archived in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Task generation, selection, and content. Tasks were generated deterministically using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 targeting very_hard and extreme workflow patterns. The preregistered sampling mapping produced 200 tasks (task_count = 200) using the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 deterministic index rule; all selection indices and task manifests were fixed prior to any hosted-model calls. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies, and difficulty metadata; manifests are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Inclusion/exclusion rules were applied deterministically before model calls (token-normalized leakage checks and syntactic pre-checks); the archived run recorded no preregistered exclusions.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared and requested model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini. That file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset in the archived configuration is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider-call accounting in the execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 with stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Deterministic verifier and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the oracle. The verifier performs deterministic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, ordering constraints against required_sequence, group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules encoded in the task manifest. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 if all required invariants pass and 0 otherwise. The verifier emits per-episode validator traces (validation_before, validation_after), violation codes, and parsed_command counts; these traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Paired semantics and failed-call treatment. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for a pair begin from the identical initial candidate; any difference in final per-pair acceptance can only arise from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The preregistered missingness plan treated persistent unparsable outputs as failures in sensitivity analyses; in the archived run there were no persistent unparsables and no excluded tasks.

Statistical analysis details and exact McNemar computation. The confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar applied to the discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). Concretely, when n = n10 + n01 and k = n10, the two-sided exact McNemar p was computed as ptwo = 2 * min{BinomialCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomialCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)}. For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this gives p = 2 * min{0.5, 0.5} = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples using seed 1729; these parameters and outputs are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The primary analysis used complete_pair_primary (include only completed pairs); a sensitivity treating persistent unparsables as failures was preregistered but unnecessary here because missingness = 0.

Execution and archival guarantees. All runtime parameters (declared/requested model, maximum_attempts_per_call, adapter stage counts), per-call provider traces, task manifests, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle. Deterministic reconciliation records provider-call stage counts and pair accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). The execution manifest is the authoritative index for run artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest reports started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00. Planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call audit stage counts recorded shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, matching the preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics with at most one repair call per task).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). The archived analysis/condition_summary.csv shows baseline successes = 199, failures = 1 (success_rate = 0.995) and guarded successes = 200, failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.015] computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All numeric values match archived artifacts (analysis/results.json and CSVs).

Repair activity and diagnostic for the single discordant pair. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair stage count = 1). The repaired pair corresponds to the archived task with task_id = task-000008 (representative artifacts archived at execution/responses/task-000008-*, execution/scoring/task-000008-*). The verifier_trace for this episode indicates a multi-step ordering violation relative to the task's required_sequence (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty level = extreme). The automated repair applied a small reordering patch restoring the required_sequence; post-repair the verifier returned valid = true and violation_count = 0. Validator traces record parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and before/after normalized configurations; these artifacts are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination monitoring. The run recorded no excluded preregistered tasks; missingness summary in analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing or unscorable episodes. The contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged items. Deterministic_reconciliation provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and cache_miss_count = 201.

Exploratory diagnostics by difficulty and command count. Archived task manifests permit exploratory stratification by difficulty level, required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. In the archived sample the single failed baseline episode (the repaired case) occurred on an extreme/very_hard composite task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3, consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering constraints concentrate failure risk. The analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes the bootstrap distribution used for CI construction and the per-condition rates; the figure artifact is archived and indexed.

sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical initial candidate for every task, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that identical candidate (a repair-only effect). This estimand does not capture benefits that could arise from alternative guarded designs (independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature modulation, or mult-sample selection).

Statistical regime, power, and practical meaning. The preregistration targeted detection of roughly 10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 assuming baseline ≈45–65%. The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those assumptions, producing low realized power to detect small absolute differences and placing inference into a discrete regime where discordant counts are small integers. In such regimes exact McNemar p-values can be uninformative for rare discordant outcomes (our analysis returned p = 1.0 for n = 1 discordant), so the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] is a more informative bound on plausible effect sizes compatible with the data.

Operational implications and scope. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach; in this synthetic deterministic setting one narrowly scoped automated repair restored invariant compliance. This supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates in a deterministic synthetic task bank. It does not imply that verifier-guarded repair will correct semantic misinterpretations of intent, omissions only observable in live dataplane telemetry, or adversarially poisoned retrievals.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and single initial generation per task limit conclusions to repair effects only. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not emulate live dataplane behavior; some operational risks require live execution tests. External validity: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank constrain generalizability—multi-model and live-device studies are necessary for broader claims. Conclusion validity: the small number of discordant pairs implies large sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and recommended follow-up grounded in artifacts. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived and indexed by the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and deterministic_reconciliation.json. Reanalysis instructions (artifact-grounded): run the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl using bootstrap_seed = 1729 and bootstrap_resamples = 10000 to reproduce the bootstrap CI. Recommended next steps (artifact-driven): (1) run independent-first-pass guarded contrasts to estimate guarded-prompt effects; (2) evaluate multiple models to assess cross-model generality; (3) expand task diversity and include live-device emulation or dataplane tests; (4) add adversarial contamination experiments. Each recommendation follows from observed limitations recorded in the archived run (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, limited adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation (task-000008). The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
